lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Experience is not arranged in reverse chronological order.
items.because: Crestline appears above the more recent, more relevant Harbor Payments internship.

items.says: The move from product-focused MBA work to Diesel Mechanic is an unexplained career pivot.
items.because: Recruiters may question whether the candidate is still pursuing product or operations roles.

items.says: Education leads even though the professional track record is the stronger qualification.
items.because: Leading with Education makes the résumé feel student-first.

items.says: “Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes” does not identify the technical approach used.
items.because: The reader cannot assess the diagnostic, overhaul or repair expertise behind the work.

items.says: “Under 5 days per job” lacks a comparison that establishes improvement.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether five days beat a prior turnaround, target or industry expectation.

items.says: “Rebuilt” uses past tense for a current role without making clear that the work was a completed initiative.
items.because: It can make the role appear finished or the date status look stale.

items.says: “Maintained hydraulic winch systems” does not specify the maintenance or repair performed.
items.because: A technical reader cannot judge the depth of the mechanical responsibility.

items.says: “For the harbor authority’s annual inspections” gives the records’ purpose rather than an achieved result.
items.because: The bullet ends on administration instead of demonstrated value.

items.says: “Maintained” and “logged” use past tense for duties presented as ongoing.
items.because: The tense conflicts with “Present” and can suggest the work has stopped.

items.says: The detailed Diesel Mechanic bullets take space without supporting the product and operations direction.
items.because: Extensive repair detail competes with more relevant evidence and can suggest an unexplained change in direction.

items.says: “The monthly review meeting that discussed them” ends with discussion rather than what the reviews changed.
items.because: Without a decision or performance consequence, the meeting reads as administrative overhead.

items.says: “Owned” frames the scorecards as a duty rather than identifying the candidate’s action.
items.because: It does not say whether the candidate produced, analyzed or improved the reporting.

items.says: “Weekly carrier scorecards” does not identify what was measured or analyzed.
items.because: The reader cannot distinguish substantive performance analysis from routine report administration.

items.says: “Two sites” is inconsistent with the entry’s numeral style.
“S&OP” is used without being defined.
“Forecast error from 18% to 11%” does not identify the error metric.
The 1,800-hour saving is buried behind a long implementation description.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the strongest evidence of value.

items.says: The entry’s strongest quantified bullet is not positioned first.
items.because: Leading with the saving would establish scope and value before less differentiated responsibilities.

items.says: “Which saved” can attribute the saving only to the telematics contract.
items.because: The saving appears to result from the broader rollout, procedures and training.

items.says: The implementation clause is overloaded with three lengthy process descriptions.
items.because: The list delays the result and gives routine execution details equal weight with the impact.

items.says: Scoring Reach as predicted support-ticket closures incorrectly applies standard RICE Reach.
items.because: Reach counts eligible users, accounts or events in a defined period; expected closures incorporate effectiveness and can double-count Impact.

items.says: “Prioritized the dispute roadmap” does not identify the decision or intended outcome.
items.because: A product hiring manager cannot tell which initiative was elevated or what problem it addressed.

items.says: The ticket-based Reach description omits the estimate, time period and evidence used.
“RICE” is unexplained jargon.
“Set the next quarter’s roadmap priority” is buried after four research and analysis activities.
items.because: The reader must process the method before learning that it influenced a roadmap decision.

items.says: “Set the next quarter’s roadmap priority” does not identify what became the priority.
items.because: The reader cannot connect the research to a concrete product direction.

items.says: “Sizing the loss by segment” omits the financial analysis’s result.
items.because: Without the magnitude, the phrase records an activity rather than its decision value.

items.says: A test randomized by session incorrectly attributes its estimated effect to merchants’ customers.
items.because: Customers can create multiple sessions and encounter both variants, so session-level assignment identifies a session-level effect.

items.says: “5-point conversion lift” does not specify percentage points, checkout conversion or the control.
items.because: The result is ambiguous and less precise than the 61%-to-66% result elsewhere.

items.says: The checkout A/B test bullet repeats the experiment and five-point lift already reported earlier.
items.because: It consumes space without adding a second accomplishment and splits the result from the experimental detail.

items.says: “Launched a surplus-food pickup app” does not show what the candidate personally owned as product lead.
items.because: The result does not distinguish the candidate’s leadership from the broader team’s work.

items.says: “To 3,100 students” does not establish whether the figure means users, registrations or eligible reach.
items.because: Those interpretations imply materially different levels of adoption.

items.says: “That would have been thrown away” is unnecessarily wordy.
“150% increase” is mathematically wrong for a rise from 400 to 1,150.
items.because: The increase is 750 users, or 187.5% of the original 400.

items.says: “By 20%” incorrectly describes the change from a 75% fill rate to 95%.
items.because: The absolute change is 20 percentage points; the relative increase is approximately 26.7%.

items.says: “Setting up a volunteer shift system” is too broad to explain how the fill rate improved.
“$2.4M annual saving” lacks a cost baseline or operating scenario for comparison.
items.because: The reader cannot evaluate the saving relative to current costs or the existing clinic-by-clinic model.

items.says: “Based on the model” does not identify the analysis behind the saving estimate.
items.because: The model’s approach or inputs would demonstrate analytical skill and make the estimate easier to assess.

items.says: “Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped” hides the candidate’s role and assessment method.
items.because: The reader cannot distinguish hands-on process analysis from general team participation.

items.says: Front-desk adoption does not show what the shorter form improved.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it reduced intake time, errors or administrative burden.

items.says: The approved scheduling pilot repeats the pilot funding outcome in the first bullet.
items.because: Both bullets culminate in the same client decision without adding a separate result.

items.says: “Presented the final recommendation” does not identify the recommendation or its analytical basis.
items.because: The line shows presentation rather than what the candidate advocated.

items.says: “Two clinics” is inconsistent with the entry’s numeral style.
items.because: The same entry uses “4 clinics.”
